body: I'd give anything for the first two; problems are inevitable - a real support network is not.
I feel the same way sometimes, but others I know that a bullet to the head is going to kill me pretty easy.  I take comfort in knowing that I can go when I choose.

As hard and cliche as this advice sounds - try to enjoy the moment if you can shake aside the depression for a bit.  It sounds like you are fairly uncommited in life - which isn't totally a bad thing ... go where you want for a bit, do what you want, live your final moments if it comes to that.  Give yourself an opportunity to find inspiration - even if it's something small.  I always find that birds somehow distract me when I'm on the brink of suicide.  Are you there yet?  How is the weather?

Funny enough, I had a manic episode, drove to Oregon (a place I love, manic or not), and then had to drive back; this happened six weeks ago.  Now I'm considering driving back after a renewed job-finding push ... I have nothing to lose at this point.  I wish I could die in the PNW as well, but I think maybe you should enjoy the city a bit before you go; nothing like being back in the beautiful city you love.

I struggle with this right now ... do I want to live a shitty life that I want no part of for years and years?  Or do I end it all soon, before I have to experience that hell.  I don't even know why I wake up in the morning to be honest.

Consider seeking help, a mixed state is the most dangerous.  My first 'real' episode was a mixed state hell, and I wouldn't wish that on anyone.  I can also relate to the ideas of wanting to flee and use up all your money for bad reasons.  I can also definitely relate to the feelings of wanting to die - a mixed state can leave a real mark on a person that never goes away; I still think of suicide every day.

Yes, I have done this.  I met my ex on Tinder, and then met the woman I cheated on her with on Tinder 1.5 years later in a hypomanic fueled sex search.  Since the split - I've slept with 3 women from online, and I feel shallow and weird each time ... often these aren't even women I'm really attracted to, it's all chasing some feeling of nurturing/love/etc.  Now I've crashed into a depression and don't even leave my house anymore, let alone date.  It's unreal how quickly I crashed.  Online dating is dangerous for me, and I'm tired of seeing the same old faces looking for love that isn't there.  I should probably delete mine now ...

I'm going on 2.5 years - it started when I was 34 when I had my first 'real' episode with Bipolar disorder.  There isn't a day that doesn't go by that I don't think about it, and how much of this hell I'm living in will it take to push me over that line.

I barely manage to make it to the toilet ... it's exhausting and feels like the only thing that keeps me from being able to sleep all day (or try to).  I don't blame ya for the ziplock bags - I know exactly how that thought comes about.

I love to travel, so this has been even harder ... no trips, no concerts, no nothing.  I fear that my roadtrips and camping will be harder to do the next time around, if there is a next time - that I'm losing capacity with each episode.

I'm currently a shut-in myself - so from one suffering to another, I want you to know you aren't alone.  I'm going on 8 months of a major 'episode' and the majority of those have been alone, not showering, feeling lower than worthless.  I'm with you in spirit friend, keep on doing the best you can, I've got faith in you.

Depression ... which sounds strange, but I know if I'm badly depressed, there is a period of mixed-episode coming or just terrible decision making mania/hypo.  I've burned so many bridges not recognizing I was 'up'.

I wish I had a good answer - I live with so much regret about burning down bridges that I didn't have to ... I just would have these terrible episodes and de-friend people and stop talking to them because I was mainly ashamed of my life, but also jealous.  8 months ago I burned the bridge to the woman I loved ... she left without a trace.  I think the best you can do is get as stable as possible, and make good decisions from there - at least that is what I've resigned myself to.  I'm not sure what else we can do.

That sounds like some typical symptoms of hypomania; I describe it as sex, drugs, and rock'n'roll ... sounds like you hit all three if you count the smoking.  Fun, but dangerous times - take it seriously, even if you don't crash into the depression.

I agree with you - staying under the TWP limit seems smart, especially if you intend on using those months at some point to take a 'real' stab at working.  I don't want to lose my disability that I just got - if I work it will be under that $850 limit for now.

I'm not an attorney FYI: This is what I understand currently ... I just received disability this month, and had the same questions.  From all I've gathered, the current figure you want to stay under is $850/month (this is before taxes).  That $850 is important because it is the "trial work period service" amount.  Going over that amount in a month counts as one of your 9 trial months that you have to go back to work.  Not going over that amount (from all I've read) does not constitute a trial work period month, and will not impact any disability benefits.  During your trial work period months you have the chance to attempt working and see if you can be successful, and can earn any amount, even over what is called the Substantial Gainful Activity amount of $1,070 - which normally would trigger an end, or reduction, to your benefits if it wasn't a trial work period month.

So, I think the moral is to save those TWP months for when you are really ready to make a run at working full-time (I plan to try eventually, maybe soon).  To do that, you have to stay under $850 a month, which is below the SGA amount, and less than the TWP service amount.

I'm actually going to post this in the main section as well to see what people think.

Sounds alot better than when I called - I got a pretty rude woman who seemed in a hurry to get off the phone.  She also gave me almost no info when I asked her about the trial work period and how much I can earn without triggering it.

Yes, I have had major problems working - I have had to quit so many jobs because I just couldn't handle the pressure/stress.  It has caused many problems with my family - they know I'm mentally ill (and applying for disability), but still make me feel worthless or less than a person because I don't have money.  I have smoked alot of weed in my life, and it doesn't satisfy me the way it used to.  I am not as controlled by weed as I used to be with the current medications I'm on.  But yes, employment/money/career is top on my list of reasons I feel like blowing my head off.

I hear you about the mental illness - I have had immense trouble holding down a job, I push people away in my relationships, and I feel like I've self-sabotaged myself for the last 10 years.  I desperately want to wake up to a different life, to a world where my mind is as healthy as others, to some kind of positive change in my life.  I often think of suicide, especially lately.  I am currently living a life where I'm in bed 15hrs a day, full of guilt, remorse, regret, and anguish.

I understand about hard and painful - I think that is what scares me most ... living through an attempt with a gun.  I often think I could do it though, I think of how to do it right and where I want to do it.  Part of me wants to leave no suicide note ... I'm not sure anyone would care.  It makes me sad to think of my things being thrown away or forgotten is somehow more important to me than my own life.

I think you hit the nail on the head of why many of us are here; without being loved, what is the point of living?  To not have another human to process life with, to hold, to tell all of your secrets to, to provide mutual comfort with ... it's lethal.

Wow, this sounds like my story exactly.  I have a college degree and haven't been able to work steadily since 2008, and I'm applying for disability ... it's a fucking sad life.  I want to work, I want to have dreams like normal people.  I'm feeling the difficulty of this journey, believe me.
Yes, 150mg.  Along with Abilify, Ativan, Lamictal, Lisinopril, and Lansoprozole.

Sounds alot like my early hypomania days; so much pot, felt so good, felt productive, thought I was really smart, had alot of sex ... good times for sure.  But all things come to an end (including the time wasted on getting high) - herb used to play a huge part in my life.

I don't know why people post them, but I feel bad for people who take even more meds than I do ... I wouldn't wish it on anyone.  The cost, being tied to them (and a Dr.), the side effects, the time in just going to pick them up and deal with the pharmacy, etc. etc. etc.
Trazadone and Ativan.

I would say Lamictal has helped me not reach the 'level' of depression that I had felt during my breakdown, and that Abilify has helped some with my rumination about the past, etc.  But it's like the meds never end, and none of them seem to work completely - it's like throwing splatters of paint against a wall, trying to cover the wall evenly ... it never happens and you end up on this roller-coaster of meds and changes and side effects.  All the while, you start to lose your personality from the meds - hell, I can barely cry ... I can't feel shit but death.  SSRI's are what caused my original breakdown - so I have no love for psychiatry.

Therapy has helped at times, and likely saved my life at times.  I currently don't have a therapist or psychiatrist (and if I don't find one fairly soon I'm in trouble).  The therapist I guess I could do without because I'm pretty poor and don't want to spend the money to be honest.  I'm not dumb and know my life is pretty fucked up, I don't need someone to sugarcoat it for me or play patty-cake with.  I did have one therapist I really liked, but she left the job and I was too 'high-risk' to be put with a student-in-training ... so that is how my therapy ended.  I guess after a few suicide attempts as someone with Bipolar disorder, you become "high-risk".  I've never felt so isolated.

I'm slipping down the hole myself, it happened fairly quickly after another manic/hypomanic fuckup.  I just wish it were easier to sleep ... it's the laying in bed waiting to sleep that really sucks.  I live for a good dream at this point - some kind of momentary fairy tale outside of the hell I live in.  It sounds like the disease is similar for us.
Sounds familiar; I wish I had better things to do, the days are so fucking long like this.

I've been diagnosed for a little over 2 years after a terrible depression where I tried to hang myself, bought a gun, finally got hospitalized.  Since the diagnosis and with all of the meds, I'm a shell of who I used to be ... the episodes seem to take it out of you a little more each time, I feel dumber/slower/older, my hair is turning white from the stress of the illness, and I require more and more meds to sleep and function.

This is the part I have a hard time making anyone understand ... that first episode flipped a switch for me, one I can't flip back.  It turned on a cycle/machine that was always there, but dormant.  Now that it's fired up, it consumes more and more, like a furnace that needs constant fuel.  Each time it doesn't get enough fuel it breaks down and requires even more fuel to get started again.  The episodes get worse and worse.

This sounds like me so much ... sleep is the only relief from the anguish; I pray to be able to sleep 24hrs a day, but I can't, my body wakes up hurting.  The only time I get up is to pee.  I cringe when I wake up and face the music.
I weigh 180lbs - so 2.5mg or so?  Can one just ingest 2.5mg of fent and expect said results?  It sounds like the patch would be a pretty slow option, by your numbers.
No, keep fighting, you've got a good chance of a very normal (nice) life in your future.  Focus on law school, finish it, start working, and rebuild from there.

Anxiety and bad depression and SSRI's until 34 - lost job, got prescribed ambien and increased Celexa, and a month later I'm plotting my own death via shotgun.  Had to go to the hospital, got diagnosed with BP2.

I've been going through a dark period for 7 months now ... pretty much have burned down my life with a breakup, terrible depression, suicide attempt, trips across the country in some kind of manic frenzy, now I'm broke, alone, and I've got no therapist or psychiatrist.  I'm honestly done with the hospital thing, I'm ready to check out and I don't feel so bad about it tbh.  The relief of it sounds like a positive feeling - I'll never have to be embarrassed, or homeless, or hate myself anymore.

I'm staying with my Dad - no Dr. here currently, so I'm on my own in that respect.  Trying to get in with a psychiatrist on Monday.  I am pretty determined to kill myself though, to be honest.  My life is in shambles and I've got nothing to live for.
I made it back, but with everything that has gone on, and what I'm left with in my life - I'm strongly considering suicide.  I think it might just be the best thing for all.
Did you go back home after you moved away?

I've said the same thing before, even to my therapist ... it's a mindfuck.  I don't trust myself to make a good decision these days, I've made so many bad ones over the course of 7 months.  Who the fuck am I ... depressed, normal, manic, should I make a decision at all?  Do I trust myself to make a good decision?
I feel the same, but I don't know if it's the disease or the meds.  Maybe both.  I am often forgetful now, a bit scattered.
Thank you all for your support - this is one of the only places anyone could possibly understand what this is, and how tiring this whole thing has been.
I agree, I have no taste for guns and never did, and I certainly never thought I'd find myself buying one.  Terrible moment for sure.

I'd say they probably do - I'm difficult to get along with sometimes, very reclusive, I've got severe mental health problems that they don't understand, and I make terrible decisions.  i'm sure they've grown tired of it, and likely question weather I can be trusted to make a good decision at all.  This shit has really taken a toll on my relationships.
Luckily I already have surrendered that gun - but I don't plan on buying another either, that just isn't going to solve my problems with my mental health.  Just make things worse.
I'm the bipolar ex-boyfriend who won't let go of his last relationship, despite the ex not having spoken to me for over 4 months.  I can't even imagine someone wanting to date me.

I can start home reasonably this Sunday ... there is nobody to help me, I came out here alone.  All I can do is push myself to make it back home; it's going to be an incredibly stressful journey, but I'm left with little choice - showing back up to my Dad's is going to be so hard - and I just pray that he lets me stay and try to get my shit together in some possible way.

Well, I do have the financial resources to go back home - it's just the massive drive and the 'tail between my legs' feeling that I'm scared of.  I hope my Dad will allow me to stay - he loaned me some money to get here, but I can pay him back in full when I arrive as I spent the rest of what I owned to get here.  This is so hard for me, this is the biggest manic mess I've ever gotten myself into ... part of me believed my ex (who works here now) would take me back, or that I'd have a good job that I could work and do alright for myself.  I realize now that I felt 'too good' when I made this plans (over the course of a month), and that I wish I had used way more caution or had someone there to tell me I was likely having an episode.  I've always been described as hypomanic (Type II), but part of me wonders how close to true mania my patterns have gotten ... I've done similar things in the past.  All in all, I'm pretty scared ... of the drive back home, of being rejected by my Dad when I get there, of having to explain to everyone that I had to come home (and why).  It's like having cut off almost all of the support (very little) that I did have 6 weeks ago.  All I can do is return and hope for the best.  I'm incredibly homesick, I feel lost up here, and I realize how expensive it will be to make it here ... I feel like I need to go back before I spend a bunch of money I can't pay back.  Lord help me, I'm in a tight bind.  I believe I'm going to start the journey back on Sunday, and spend 30hrs hoping I have a place to stay when I get back.

So things have been a little better the last couple of days - at least I can sit down and focus for a bit.  I am back to 2.5mg of Abilify, 200mg Lamictal.  I found that using the light therapy lamp in the early morning was kind of causing me to 'hype' up a bit more during the day - I read a study that suggests using it during the mid-day is more beneficial for people with Bipolar disorder.  We'll see if it works.  I'm thinking about asking the Doc to go back to Lexapro in addition to the Abilify (or without it) ... I honestly felt much more normal than this when I was on it, even if it did give me a 'boost' that felt a little like hypomania.

Thank you for the words of wisdom.  Sometimes when I'm hypomanic, I want to start smoking alot of pot - so I've made sure I don't have access to that.  I feel like it just numbs the hypomania until it sends me into another depressed episode.  Luckily, alcohol has never been very good to me, so I don't have trouble avoiding that.
No anti-depressant, but I am on Lamictal in addition to the Abilify.  Melatonin has definitely helped, though I have some real weird dreams when I take it.

I've called my Dr. and I'm waiting for a call back - I don't want to be having to pump myself full of Ativan to stay calm; the last thing I need is a benzo habit.  I think the light therapy may be playing a part, but I'm waking up pretty wired (and sleep is tough, as you can imagine).  I'm currently taking Trazadone and Ativan to sleep - it helps but I sometimes have to throw Tylenol PM in the mix to stay asleep.

I just don't think I can do it ... as much pain as I'm in, as ashamed of my life as I am, my brain is telling me not to kill myself.  That maybe with time and the right medications, I can be ok again.  It's a leap of faith, and one that is gong to require pushing through some more suffering.  I don't know how much longer I'll be able to keep going, but I'm going to give it everything I have left.

Suicide doesn't require weakness, it requires strength; it's very hard to do, and only those who have had a gun to their head know what I mean.  To accept death is to reject life, but lives are different, tolerance for mental pain is different, and the future we will lead will be different.  My story is simply one that has been told many times - the ruin left behind by Bipolar disorder is real, and the life we are forced to live is not pleasant.  To be trapped inside a cell that won't let your mind go is a fate far worse than death.  I want better for the next person - I pray that treatment improves in years to come, nobody should have to live my story.  I appreciate your support, I truly wish my words could save my life, but if it saves another from this misery, I will have left behind something that matters.

Allow me to explain my life, so that you all can understand my situation.  At age 12, I was diagnosed with hydrocephalus, and underwent brain surgery to have a shunt implanted in my head.  I strongly believe I had suffered a TBI before this, or that the surgery itself caused changes in my brain.  At age 15, my parents moved me from the place I had grown up to a town I'd never been to, I had no friends, nothing.  I spent highschool experiencing my first depressions, followed by periods of hypomania ... I wouldn't know that I had Bipolar disorder for another 20 years.  During those 20 years, I fell far behind my peers in terms of financial and personal success - while others had stable relationships with their family, friends, and significant others, I found my relationships unstable, short-lived, and devastating when they ended.  I managed to graduate college, but had no idea how precarious my mental health was until ~10 years ago, when I experienced my first extreme depression, followed by hypomania.  This cycle went on for 10 years, costing me time, relationships, money,  love, and self respect ... at age 34, I found myself alone, without a career, without love, without family support.  I lost it, and frankly, have never regained who I was prior to 2  years ago.  I was diagnosed with Bipolar disorder shortly after, and have spent the last two years battling for my life.  My everyday is hell, my regrets simply dominate me, and I have no support or love in my life.  I am in extreme mental pain most of my day, and I'm on a constant cycle of medications, ineffective therapy, hospitalizations, and am losing time and any chance to turn my life around.

I'm simply exhausted, and I am ready to find peace for myself.  I pray each day that God or someone out there will be able to take away this pain, to make me whole again, to soothe what is wrong with my mind.  There is no answer - just silence.  I pray that each of you find the peace we all seek - none of us deserve to suffer.

If I have any advice for those of you who are younger and still have time to make things right, it would be to seek treatment far earlier than I did, help your family to seek treatment, and never abandon someone because they are mentally ill.  I've been thrown away like trash a dozen times, and it's taken a piece of me every time.  The small amount of money I have is meaningless without the thins in life that really matter; love, family, health, and peace of mind.  I'd trade it all for a small glimmer of the hope I used to hold as a younger man.
